correctness.rationale: Three families of sixteen lines give a sharp twelve-line upper bound (at most four from each family). Each four-line group corresponds to a permutation of four distinct eighth-root slopes (24 possibilities), and exactly all 13,824 triples are enumerated using exact determinants over Z[t]/(t^4+1). A separate rank test over F17 agrees for each of 1,128 line pairs. Full projective monomiality follows from the Hessian coordinate-hyperplane divisor, and six generating transformations produce orbit sizes 32 and 96. Full Gal(Q(zeta8)/Q) action gives fixed counts 128,16,128,16, implying 16 rational sets and 112 minimally Q(i)-defined sets. The included verifier completed with VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: Classifying all maximum-cardinality skew-line systems on a classical quartic refines a natural optimization problem studied in the originating paper, rather than recomputing its upper bound. The 32/96 geometric symmetry split identifies two structurally distinct extremal configurations. The fact that every unordered 12-line divisor descends to Q(i) and 16 descend to Q, despite none of the 48 constituent lines being defined over Q(i), is a substantive arithmetic descent phenomenon with relevance to rational divisor configurations. These invariants concern the complete natural object, not an arbitrary slice.
